gaps.concept: Primary spermatocytes are diploid with replicated DNA; meiosis I produces haploid secondary spermatocytes, and meiosis II produces haploid spermatids.
gaps.why_tested: A diagram asks for chromosome or DNA content at a specified stage of spermatogenesis.

gaps.concept: Sperm acquire motility in the epididymis; capacitation and the acrosome reaction later enable penetration of the oocyte.
gaps.why_tested: An infertility stem asks why sperm leaving the testis cannot yet fertilize an oocyte.

gaps.concept: The blood–testis barrier protects postpubertal germ-cell antigens from immune recognition; disruption can cause antisperm antibodies.
gaps.why_tested: Infertility follows testicular trauma despite otherwise preserved hormone production.

gaps.concept: Inhibin B selectively suppresses FSH; testosterone provides negative feedback predominantly on GnRH and LH.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks which gonadotropin rises after isolated seminiferous tubule injury.

gaps.concept: Continuous GnRH agonist exposure suppresses LH and FSH after an initial surge; pulsatile GnRH stimulates their release.
gaps.why_tested: A pharmacology stem asks why continuous GnRH administration reduces testicular testosterone.

gaps.concept: Exogenous testosterone or anabolic steroids suppress LH and FSH, lowering intratesticular testosterone and causing testicular atrophy and infertility.
gaps.why_tested: A muscular patient has azoospermia, small testes, and low gonadotropins.

gaps.concept: Primary testicular failure causes low testosterone with elevated LH and FSH; hypothalamic or pituitary failure causes low testosterone with low gonadotropins.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone panel must localize the cause of hypogonadism.

gaps.concept: Isolated seminiferous tubule damage causes low inhibin B and high FSH with relatively preserved testosterone and LH.
gaps.why_tested: An infertile man has normal virilization but a selectively elevated FSH level.

gaps.concept: Kallmann syndrome causes GnRH deficiency with anosmia, delayed puberty, low LH and FSH, and low testosterone.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with absent smell and delayed sexual development has hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

gaps.concept: Hyperprolactinemia inhibits GnRH, reducing LH, FSH, testosterone, libido, and fertility.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with sexual dysfunction and elevated prolactin has low gonadotropins.

gaps.concept: 47,XXY Klinefelter syndrome causes small firm testes, azoospermia, gynecomastia, low testosterone, high gonadotropins, and hyalinized seminiferous tubules.
gaps.why_tested: A tall infertile man has small testes and a hypergonadotropic hormone pattern.

gaps.concept: Y-chromosome AZF-region microdeletions impair spermatogenesis and cause severe oligospermia or nonobstructive azoospermia.
gaps.why_tested: A man has azoospermia despite palpable ducts and no obvious acquired testicular injury.

gaps.concept: CFTR variants can cause congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens, producing obstructive azoospermia with preserved testicular sperm production.
gaps.why_tested: An infertile man has nonpalpable vasa deferentia and otherwise preserved testicular function.

gaps.concept: Obstructive azoospermia usually has normal testicular size and FSH; impaired sperm production often has small testes and elevated FSH.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks whether absent sperm reflects duct obstruction or testicular failure.

gaps.concept: Ejaculatory duct obstruction or absent seminal vesicles can produce low-volume, acidic semen lacking fructose.
gaps.why_tested: An azoospermic patient has little ejaculate with low pH and absent seminal-vesicle markers.

gaps.concept: Vasectomy blocks sperm delivery without stopping testosterone production or substantially reducing semen volume.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which reproductive functions persist after division of the vas deferens.

gaps.concept: Cryptorchidism exposes an undescended testis to excess heat, impairing spermatogenesis and increasing testicular germ-cell tumor risk.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with a history of an undescended testis presents with infertility or a testicular mass.

gaps.concept: A left varicocele reflects impaired left testicular venous drainage into the left renal vein; it feels like a bag of worms and can impair fertility.
gaps.why_tested: An infertile man has dilated scrotal veins that enlarge while standing.

gaps.concept: The right testicular vein drains to the inferior vena cava; the left drains to the left renal vein.
gaps.why_tested: An anatomy or varicocele stem asks which vein receives testicular drainage.

gaps.concept: Testicular lymph drains to para-aortic nodes, whereas scrotal skin drains to superficial inguinal nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks where a testicular versus scrotal lesion first spreads.

gaps.concept: Testicular torsion twists the spermatic cord, causing sudden pain, a high-riding transverse testis, absent cremasteric reflex, and reduced Doppler flow.
gaps.why_tested: An acute scrotal-pain stem asks for the mechanism or distinguishing finding.

gaps.concept: The cremasteric reflex has an ilioinguinal nerve sensory limb and a genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve motor limb.
gaps.why_tested: A nerve-injury or torsion question asks for the reflex pathway.

gaps.concept: A patent processus vaginalis permits a communicating hydrocele; a fluid-filled hydrocele typically transilluminates.
gaps.why_tested: An infant has painless scrotal swelling that changes size or transilluminates.

gaps.concept: Sympathetic T11–L2 activity mediates emission and bladder-neck closure; pudendal S2–S4 contractions expel semen during ejaculation.
gaps.why_tested: A neurologic lesion disrupts ejaculation while erection remains possible.

gaps.concept: Erection compresses venous outflow from the corpora cavernosa; the corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and remains less rigid.
gaps.why_tested: A penile anatomy question asks how tumescence is maintained while the urethra remains patent.

gaps.concept: PDE5 inhibitors prolong cGMP signaling and can cause severe hypotension when combined with nitrates.
gaps.why_tested: An erectile-dysfunction drug stem asks for its mechanism or a dangerous interaction.

gaps.concept: SRD5A2 deficiency lowers DHT and raises the testosterone:DHT ratio; 46,XY patients retain Wolffian structures but have undervirilized external genitalia and pubertal virilization.
gaps.why_tested: An adolescent with ambiguous genitalia at birth virilizes at puberty despite male internal ducts.

gaps.concept: Complete androgen insensitivity causes a 46,XY female external phenotype, absent Müllerian and Wolffian structures, testes, and elevated testosterone and LH.
gaps.why_tested: Primary amenorrhea with a blind-ending vagina and absent uterus must be distinguished from 5α-reductase deficiency.

gaps.concept: SRY initiates testis differentiation; Sertoli-cell AMH causes Müllerian duct regression, while Leydig-cell testosterone maintains Wolffian ducts.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology stem asks which fetal signal is absent when specific internal reproductive structures persist or regress.

gaps.concept: Finasteride inhibits 5α-reductase, lowering DHT; adverse effects include reduced libido and erectile or ejaculatory dysfunction.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops sexual adverse effects after treatment targeting androgen-dependent prostate growth or hair loss.

gaps.concept: Efferent ductules have a scalloped lumen from alternating ciliated and absorptive cells; the vas deferens has a thick muscular wall and folded lumen.
gaps.why_tested: A histology image asks which sperm-transport duct is shown.

gaps.concept: Seminal vesicles have highly folded glandular mucosa and normally contain secretions without sperm.
gaps.why_tested: A histology section of an accessory gland must be distinguished from a sperm-containing duct.
